note: Original content written for Roll Ready. Entries: "text" or [weight, "text"]. {key} rolls another table, {key x3} rolls three different entries, {2d6*10} rolls dice.

tables.name: Rumor
entries: The miller swears the river ran backward for an hour at the last new moon.
Someone has been paying the gravedigger to leave one plot empty.
A merchant caravan arrived on time with every wagon full and no drivers.
The old watchtower has a light in it again, and nobody holds the key.
Wolves have been seen walking the road in pairs, calm as pilgrims.
The baker's new apprentice never seems to show in the shop window's reflection.
A stranger is buying up every map of the hills, no matter how wrong it is.
The well in the square tasted of salt for three days, then of honey.
Two rival families both claim to have found the same lost ring.
A bounty was posted for a beast, then quietly taken down the next morning.
The ferryman won't cross after dusk since something knocked on the hull from below.
The children have a new skipping rhyme, and nobody knows who taught it to them.
The temple bell rang thirteen at midnight. The priest says it only has twelve in it.
A tinker is selling keys he says fit doors that haven't been built yet.
Sheep on the high pasture have been found shorn in the night, neat as you please.
The tax collector went into the marsh village and came back cheerful. That never happens.
There's a cellar under the cooper's shop that the cooper insists isn't there.
A hooded traveler paid for a week's lodging in coins no one recognizes.
Hunters found a ring of standing stones where there was open meadow last spring.
The deepest shaft of the mine was sealed, and it was sealed from the inside.
Crows keep gathering on one rooftop, and the family there has stopped answering the door.
A statue in the square has turned to face the other way.
Somebody is leaving fresh flowers at the crossroads every dawn.
The mapmakers are quietly hiring guards who don't ask questions.

tables.name: Treasure: CR 0–4
entries: {3d6} gp and {4d6} sp in a worn pouch

tables.name: Shop stock (flavor)
entries: a dusty rack of walking sticks
hand-drawn local maps of doubtful accuracy
a locked case of “genuine” lucky charms
smoked sausages hanging from the rafters

tables.name: Shop quirks
entries: The owner haggles only in rhyme.
Everything is priced in odd numbers.
A very old dog is asleep across the doorway.
The shop closes without warning whenever it rains.
The owner insists on wrapping every purchase, however small.
A hand-lettered sign reads: No credit, no songs.
The owner is certain they have met one of the party before.
Half the shelves are labeled in a script nobody else reads.
There is a second, smaller door behind the counter that is never mentioned.
The owner pays well for gossip from out of town.

tables.name: Valuables: modest
entries: a silver ring set with a chip of garnet (about 15 gp)
a brass spyglass with a cracked lens (10 gp)
a bolt of fine blue linen (12 gp)
a set of loaded dice (2 gp, more to the right buyer)
a pewter flask engraved with a ship (8 gp)
a finely painted toy knight (5 gp)
a copper bracelet shaped like a fish (6 gp)
an inlaid wooden game board (20 gp)
a small bronze bell with a sweet tone (9 gp)

tables.name: Valuables: fine
entries: a gold locket holding a lock of grey hair (75 gp)
a matched pair of moonstones (100 gp)
a jade figurine of a heron (150 gp)
a ledger of debts owed by local notables (50 gp for the binding, far more as leverage)
a small painting in a gilt frame (200 gp)
a set of silver table knives (90 gp)
an amber pendant with an insect inside (130 gp)

tables.name: Valuables: exceptional
entries: a circlet of white gold set with sapphires (2,500 gp)
a ceremonial sword with a ruby pommel (1,800 gp)
a tapestry woven with gold thread (1,200 gp)
a star ruby the size of a thumbnail (1,000 gp)
a crystal decanter and six goblets (900 gp)
a properly sealed deed to a vineyard (3,000 gp to the right claimant)
a carved obsidian mask with opal eyes (2,000 gp)
a platinum signet ring of an extinct house (1,500 gp)
a jeweled music box that plays an unfamiliar tune (2,200 gp)
a string of black pearls (4,000 gp)

tables.name: Who they are: City
entries: Night-shift lamplighter who sees everything after dark
Customs clerk with a stamp for every occasion
Rat-catcher who names the ones that get away
Pawnbroker who never forgets a face or a debt
Ferry pilot who knows every sandbar and every bribe
Street cook with one famous dish and one feared one
Junior guild scribe drowning in paperwork
Off-duty watch sergeant nursing sore feet
Chimney sweep who hears conversations through the flues
Messenger who runs the rooftops to save time
Locksmith who swears they only open doors honestly
Bathhouse attendant who trades in overheard gossip
Bookbinder with ink to the elbows
Debt collector who hates the work
Bell-ringer from the old clock tower
Stonemason repairing the same wall for the third time

tables.name: Who they are: Village
entries: Shepherd who is down one sheep and up one mystery
Midwife who delivered half the village
Blacksmith's apprentice desperate to prove themself
Beekeeper who talks to the hives first
Travelling tinker with a cart of mended pots
Village reeve tired of settling fence disputes
Hedge-witch who sells charms that mostly work
Brewer whose last batch went strange
Gravedigger with a dry sense of humor
Carter who hauls for anyone who pays by noon
Widowed innkeeper with three empty rooms
Goose-girl who knows every path out of the valley
Itinerant preacher with a hoarse voice
Charcoal burner in from the woods for supplies

tables.name: Who they are: Wilderness or road
entries: Trapper with a string of pelts and a bad cough
Toll-keeper at a bridge nobody maintains
Pilgrim walking barefoot on a vow
Caravan guard whose caravan left without them
Surveyor mapping a road nobody asked for
Herb-gatherer with a satchel of things that should not be eaten
Deserter still wearing half a uniform
Wandering knife-sharpener with a grindstone on their back
Lost courier guarding a sealed satchel
Hermit who came down for salt
Prospector certain the next hill is the one
Drover moving stubborn cattle to market
Peddler of maps, at least half of them accurate
Storm-stranded sailor a long way from any coast
Bounty hunter comparing faces to a sketch
Circus strongman walking to the next town
Exiled noble travelling under a plain name

tables.name: Who they are: Dungeon or ruin
entries: Rival treasure-seeker separated from their crew
Prisoner who has been here longer than they can count
Scholar copying inscriptions by candle stub
Tunnel guide who claims to know a shortcut
Injured mercenary left behind by an employer
Scavenger who sells what the dead leave
Apprentice mage sent to fetch one specific thing
Miner whose shaft broke through into this place
Caretaker who still sweeps halls nobody uses
Smuggler using the lower passages as a warehouse
Cartographer three sheets into a map and one torch from the dark
Runaway hiding where nobody would look
Grave-priest come to lay something to rest
Captured scout waiting for a chance to bolt
Mushroom farmer who likes the quiet

tables.name: Who they are: Noble court
entries: Under-steward who actually runs the household
Third child of a minor house with nothing to inherit
Court musician with a new and risky ballad
Royal food-taster with a nervous stomach
Lady's companion who reads all the letters first
Master of hounds who trusts dogs over courtiers
Visiting envoy far from home and short on allies
Dance tutor who hears every whisper on the floor
Disgraced knight seeking one more audience
Portrait painter kept waiting for a month
Court astrologer whose predictions keep coming true
Page who knows the servant stairs
Tax assessor nobody invites to dinner
Dowager with a long memory and a short temper

tables.name: Who they are: Underworld
entries: Fence who only deals in things that fit in a pocket
Lookout paid by two crews at once
Bookmaker who gives honest odds on dishonest fights
Retired burglar with a bad knee
Poisoner who insists on the word apothecary
Informant who sells the same secret twice
Street-gang lieutenant barely old enough to shave
Safehouse keeper who asks no questions
Card sharp on a losing streak
Dock boss who decides which crates go missing
Disbarred advocate who defends thieves for a cut

tables.name: Appearance
entries: Ink-stained fingers and a missing eyebrow
A coat two sizes too large, sleeves rolled thick
One green eye, one grey, and a steady stare
Hair cropped unevenly, as if cut in a hurry
A scar across the chin that pulls the smile crooked
Wears three scarves regardless of weather
Carries a walking stick carved with tally marks
A fine ring on a rough hand
Tall and stooped, like someone used to low doorways
A patchwork cloak with one bright new square
Mud to the knees and spotless above
A braid threaded with small brass bells
Smells faintly of woodsmoke and cloves
A burn mark shaped like a crescent on one forearm
Grey at the temples though clearly young
Missing two fingers and gestures with the stumps
A tattoo of a knot on the side of the neck
Cheeks flushed, out of breath, hat askew
Tiny and wiry, with a voice that carries
Flour or dust on every seam
A chipped front tooth and a ready grin
Pockets that clink when they move
Eyes rimmed red from lack of sleep
A lopsided haircut hidden under a knitted cap

tables.name: Voice or mannerism
entries: Speaks in a near-whisper and leans in close
Ends every statement as if it were a question
Counts on their fingers while talking
Laughs before finishing their own jokes
Clears their throat before anything important
Talks fast and trips over long words
Long pauses, as if translating in their head
Taps the table twice to make a point
Hums the same four notes when thinking
Refers to themself by full name
Booming voice with no indoor setting
Answers a question with a different question
Keeps glancing at the nearest exit
Chews a sprig of something and talks around it
Formal to the point of stiffness; bows too often
Slow drawl, never hurried by anything
Polishes something with a sleeve while listening
Sniffs sharply at the end of each sentence
Speaks only in short, flat statements
Gestures widely and knocks things over
Lowers their voice whenever money comes up
Sing-song delivery, like reciting a rhyme
Squints as if every listener were far away
Cracks their knuckles one at a time
Repeats the last word they heard before replying

tables.name: Wants right now
entries: Someone to carry a sealed letter across town before nightfall
A safe escort to the next settlement
Enough coin to settle a debt due tomorrow
To find a missing sibling last seen nearby
A witness to back up their side of a dispute
To be left alone long enough to finish one job
A hot meal and a dry place to sleep
To get rid of an object they regret acquiring
News of the road ahead, and will pay for it
A buyer for something they should not be selling
Revenge on a rival, preferably deniable
To impress someone important who is watching
Help moving something heavy without questions
To hire muscle for one evening
To stall for time until a friend arrives
Proof that a rumor about them is false
Passage out of here under another name
To win back something lost in a wager
An introduction to someone the party knows
To return a borrowed item before it is missed
Directions, having clearly been lost for hours
To pass a message without their employer finding out
Someone to blame, and the party is convenient
A second opinion on a strange find
To keep a promise made to someone now dead
To sell information while it is still worth something
To be believed, just this once

tables.name: Secret or complication
entries: Is not who they claim to be; the real one is missing
Was paid this morning to watch for people like the party
Saw something last night and is afraid to say
Is being followed and knows it
Has a price on their head in the next province
Is secretly related to a local figure of power
Stole the thing they are trying to sell
Is spying for a faction and regretting it
Made a promise to a creature that was not human
Knows where something valuable is buried but cannot reach it alone
Recently betrayed a friend and it eats at them
Cannot read, and the letter they carry matters
Is under a minor curse that sours milk nearby
Has a twin who causes them endless trouble
Is the only survivor of something they will not discuss
Works for two employers who would kill each other
Lied on an oath and expects consequences
Is hiding a small, illegal animal in their coat
Believes, wrongly, that the party was sent to kill them
Has already sold this information to someone else
Is guarding a child's secret, not their own
Was once wealthy and is ashamed of the fall
Hears a voice giving advice, and it is usually right
Has exactly one day left before something comes due

tables.name: Hook: Friendly
entries: Recognizes a party member from a good deed and insists on repaying it
Offers a shortcut, a spare room, or a warning, free of charge
Mistakes the party for old friends and it would be awkward to correct
Has been hoping capable strangers would turn up, and says so
Presses a small gift on the party and asks only that they remember the name
Wants to hear the party's story and has one worth trading
Vouches for the party to a suspicious local without being asked
Shares a meal and lets slip something useful
Is heading the same way and would be glad of the company
Knows someone who needs exactly the party's kind of help

tables.name: Hook: Neutral
entries: Has what the party needs, at a fair price and not a copper less
Is in the party's way through no fault of their own
Will answer three questions and then has work to do
Saw the party arrive and is deciding whether that matters
Needs one small favor before they can spare any attention
Happens to be holding the thing the party is looking for
Was just about to leave, but can be persuaded to stay
Is waiting for someone else and the party will do in the meantime
Offers a straight trade: news for news
Does not care who the party is, only whether they are buying

tables.name: Hook: Hostile
entries: Blames the party for something that happened before they arrived
Has orders to keep people like the party out
Was cheated by the last group of adventurers through here
Wants what one party member is carrying and has noticed it
Is itching for a fight and the party looks like one
Considers this their territory and expects a toll
Works for someone the party has already crossed
Loudly accuses a party member of theft
Refuses to deal with outsiders and wants an audience for the refusal
Recognizes a party member from a wanted notice

tables.name: Hook: Scared
entries: Begs the party not to say they were seen here
Thinks the party was sent by the people hunting them
Flinches at loud voices and will run if cornered
Blurts out a warning and immediately regrets it
Offers everything in their purse to be escorted somewhere safe
Keeps looking over the party's shoulders at something
Has barricaded themself in and will only talk through the gap
Is clutching a bundle and will not say what is in it
Whispers that it is not safe to talk here
Wants to hire the party on the spot, no haggling

tables.name: Hook: Shady
entries: Has an offer that sounds too good and a reason to hurry
Knows something about a party member and mentions it casually
Will sell a way in, a name, or a key, with payment up front
Is clearly sizing up the party's valuables
Proposes a job with the important detail left out
Claims to speak for someone powerful and cannot quite prove it
Offers to make a problem disappear for a favor to be named later
Is selling the same map the party already bought
Steers the conversation toward where the party is staying
Slips a note into a pocket and walks away
